rv.q: Rarely does a show live up so honestly to its title — wrecking and illuminating in equal measure.
Kelly has created a vibrant and provocative piece that takes the wraps off buried homosexuality amongst black males as well as the stigmas of mental illness and depression.
I was deeply moved by Kelly’s quietly tragic ending, and I couldn’t help being reminded of a scene from the film The Hours...
Would that his writing matched the clarity and precision of his direction.
But The Fires, which is never dull, is constrained by its structure; the stage is filled with people, none of whom have enough room to breathe.
His nearly two-hour play, however, aside from a few rhapsodic moments
It’s an apt message for a stunning piece of theater.

cn.t: Choreographer Raja Feather Kelly makes a striking playwriting debut with this time-jumping drama about three Black gay men across different eras. Critics praise its movement and emotional depth, though some find the execution uneven.
